name: cc-enslaver
description: A Claude Code plugin and LLM-agnostic rule pack that enforces systematic thinking, verified citations, and root-cause analysis — eliminating reactive, lazy AI behavior. v0.28.0 upgrades rules 03 + 09 into a mandatory trace-upstream → diagnose → unified-fix discipline: when a problem appears, point-to-point patching is banned outright. Rule 03 gains an upstream tracing ladder — every failure has a symptom site, a propagation path, and an origin (the mechanism / design decision / missing invariant that generates the bad state); fixing at the first two levels is a patch even when the observed failure disappears, climbing stops only with the true origin named and the reason stated, and the diagnosis must be demonstrated by a first-party probe / reproduction / failing test BEFORE the first line of the fix is written. Rule 09 gains 'one root cause, one unified fix' — a diagnosed root cause defines a CLASS of defects, the observed instance being merely the one that surfaced first; sweep the repo for every sibling, fix the generating mechanism once covering all instances in the same pass, and prove the class is closed by re-triggering at least one OTHER instance (N symptoms with one root = one fix, never N patches). Grounded in this repo's own measured history: v0.25.1 named a root cause and fixed only the instances it had seen, the mechanism survived and regenerated a fresh crop by v0.26 including one regression — v0.28 codifies v0.26's replace-the-mechanism response as the required shape of every fix. Zero new detectors, per the v0.22.1 precedent (a reasoning shape, not a syntax shape hooks can match); the existing hard layers — patch-marker content scan, rolling-patch frequency layer, Stop layer (f) root-cause triplet — remain the physical floor. A candidate Stop-layer marker extension is recorded for the user's decision rather than shipped unilaterally. Tests hold at 556. Prior — v0.27.0 closes the three items v0.26 recorded as 'known, not fixed', each decided by evidence rather than preference. (1) The shell tokeniser now follows the SHELL, not the host OS: v0.25.1 disabled backslash escaping when os.name == 'nt', but measuring the shell Claude Code actually runs on Windows (Git Bash / MSYS, bash 5.2.37) showed the branch wrong in both directions — an unquoted drive path loses its separators in the real shell too, so it rescued nothing, while `git push --for\ce` reached git as --force with the guard seeing an unrecognised token. That live force-push bypass is closed; a drive path must be QUOTED. (2) Stop layer (h) now carries two verdicts instead of one: 'attributable' (generous, for presence — a false negative blocks a reply for a tldr that is visibly present) and 'countable' (conservative, for the 160-char measurement). They differ only on CommonMark lazy continuation, which is exactly why v0.26 could not implement it; it is implemented now. (3) Stop layer (i) settles only groups the agent has actually been SHOWN — the primary path used to ack every pending group while the grace path acked only the presented set, and that inconsistency was itself the bypass. A group is named by one block, then settled by the next reply's marker: one INFORMED answer per group. That is a strictness increase, recorded as such. Tests 543 → 556. Prior — v0.26.0 was a fourth-round audit release: it reviewed the PREVIOUS release's own fix diff and replaced the mechanism instead of the symptoms. 37 findings, 33 reproduced by first-party runtime probes, collapsing into three root causes — the detector encoded a SPELLING rather than the concept (a `#` inside a URL counted as a comment, so one neighbouring `https://api.example.com` line disabled the secret detector; block structure was read from PHYSICAL lines, which regressed nested try/except from deny to allow while claiming the opposite); hardening was scoped to the observed instance rather than the class; and the claim outran the change (four tests passed unchanged on the pre-fix tree, and the self-rewritability invariant claimed to cover the whole tree while globbing half of it — six of the ten test modules were self-locked). Fixed as four shared models — lib/srclex (tolerant source lexer: comments vs docstrings vs data literals), lib/mdctx (markdown fence/blockquote context, now shared by both halves of Stop layer (h)), lib/shellcmd (segments → argv → git subcommand / python script operand), and a schema-driven state normaliser — rather than ~30 individual patches. The fix was then RE-AUDITED before shipping and 8 further defects in the NEW code were found and fixed, one of which would have been a regression ($(git push --force) was caught by the old text heuristic purely by accident). Tests 378 → 543 across two audit rounds; the first round's 43 failures + 3 errors replay on the pre-fix tree. A SECOND round of 16 parallel read-only reviews (15 reported; the sync-gate lens returned nothing and is recorded as not run) then fixed 20+ further confirmed defects at the root — a bare triple-quoted expression counting as a docstring and so silencing the secret detector, a lone CR letting a comment swallow the rest of a file, the tldr length check ignoring line attribution on continuation lines (the same two-halves-disagree bug one level down), 'far from done' reading as a completion and BLOCKING honest failure reports, a JSONDecodeError silently wiping a session's entire state, six Bash patterns still matching raw text while force-push used a parse model, and a registration inside `false && …` earning read credit for a command the shell never runs. It also caught five stale test counts and two false claims in THIS release's own notes — the gate had exempted the current release's narrative as 'history' while it describes the release being shipped. Prior — v0.24 health audit: a full architecture review plus multi-path adversarial model review (every finding re-verified with a runtime probe; red-first regression tests, 310 → 323) fixed 10 confirmed defects, 3 HIGH, zero new features. Its HIGH fixes: Windows state saves were silently lost to the plugin's OWN lock-free readers (os.replace vs an open reader → PermissionError → failing-open → the mutation vanished, with orphan .tmp debris as live evidence; read accessors now share the per-session lock, save() retries against non-cooperating external readers, load() retries transient OSError, gc sweeps day-old orphan tmp files); the layer-(i) sync acknowledgement was lost in the one-shot grace window (the primary block → 同步核对-recovery flow never persisted the ack, so an answered group re-blocked later — the grace path now reads the reply and acks); and a DENIED Write of a new file still registered its target as 'read', granting read-before-edit authorization for content the agent never saw. MED fixes: the rolling-patch counter's decide-and-record is now one atomic locked operation; rule 10 no longer flags Python forward-reference annotations (password: "SecretStr" — pure-alpha CamelCase values are type names, not secrets); rule 11 no longer flags URL routes (https://host/home/alice/… — a hostname-glued /home/ segment is a route; file:///home/… still denies); requirements*.txt / constraints*.txt are now scannable despite .txt (dependency manifests are a real credential-leak vector) while .asciidoc joins the prose exemption; and a stale rolling counter no longer survives delete-and-recreate. The three write branches of read_guard were deduplicated into one shared content-check pipeline, making the branch-drift bug class structurally impossible. Prior: v0.23 added rule 12 (repo-wide sync: per-project sync-gate.toml co-update groups enforced at Stop layer (i) with a marker escape, plus the repo-refresh whole-repo audit skill), a 160-char-per-item TL;DR cap at layer (h), and two HIGH production fixes (edit-gated Stop layers never fired — no turn_count in production payloads; session-state lost-update race); v0.22 added write-time content detectors rules 10 (no non-essential hardcoding) and 11 (no non-essential path dependency), PreToolUse-only with a why-comment escape hatch; v0.22.2 added the version-drift gate pinning every manifest version pointer, the README badge, and the newest CHANGELOG heading to plugin.json. English remains the i18n skeleton and source of truth (rules/ + prompts/ at the root, default injection); Chinese is a first-class translation (rules/zh/ + prompts/zh/, via CC_ENSLAVER_LANG=zh), with drift CI-blocked by i18n_check.py + test_i18n_sync.py.
